classification: pre-registered Monte Carlo portfolio-parameter audit on the R377 sealed hold-30 centre; research-only
question: R370 perturbed the portfolio parameters around the R360 20-day centre. Does the R377 hold-30 centre keep its sealed-window advantage across a five-dimensional Monte Carlo of portfolio construction parameters, or is it dependent on the exact R374 values?

design.method: Latin hypercube over five portfolio-level parameters, identical spans to R370
design.pairing: each Latin-hypercube sample is applied identically to the hold-30 centre and the 20-day control

sealed_advantage.rule: centre total return > control total return on the same Monte Carlo sample

plateau.reason: A centre whose advantage disappears under most nearby portfolio parameter draws is a knife-edge, not a platform.

decision_rules: The centre is parameter-robust only if all three plateau thresholds pass.
The control is run on the same samples so that a general market-level shift cannot be mistaken for parameter robustness.
The sealed window is not used to reselect any parameter; it is only reported.
No leverage, paper target, order or production change is permitted.
known_limits: The B-sleeve curves are fixed; only portfolio construction parameters are perturbed.
The sealed window is about 17 months and overlaps the 2025-2026 regime.
The 96 Latin-hypercube samples are correlated with the original R370 audit and are not independent trials.
Current HS300 membership and industry backfill limitations remain.
